line: supervisor -- a NEW line, not a variant of the agent epoch-1/epoch-2 sweep. The agent sweep trained stage bidders to emit BID/NO_BID with a price; this trains a selector to pick one chain from a candidate list. Different task, different prompt, different metric.

data.split: order-id disjoint, 9.9% holdout, seed 42, verified overlap 0
data.labels: src.common.bidding_formulas.decide_chain_selection -- compound risk, budget-relative normalization, equal thirds for normal, urgent=min days, flexible=min cost
data.prompt: src.common.slm.build_chain_selection_prompt (the same builder the live supervisor calls)

batch.deviation_note: the agent sweep used 8x2. 4x4 is the protocol's own native-fit rule (reduce per-device, keep effective 16, disclose) and was chosen because 8x2 at 2048 probed at 21.5 GiB, which prior probe-to-run deltas suggest would spill. No sibling supervisor run exists to stay consistent with, so unlike smollm3 there is no comparison purity cost.

training.optimizer: adamw_8bit lr 2e-4 warmup 5 linear, weight_decay 0.01, bf16, seed 42

important_caveat_on_interpretation: this is a FRESH run from the base checkpoint, not the epoch-2 run truncated at step 614. The linear LR schedule spans the whole run, so at step 614 the epoch-2 run sat at ~50%% of peak LR while this one decays to ~0. The two trajectories differ from step 6 onward, which is why the comparison uses two separately trained adapters.

metrics: selection accuracy (exact index match with the rule)
regret on the strategy's own objective, as a fraction of the rule's value
evaluation.validation: on 150/150 pre-check rows the rule's stored label was the argmin of the objective the harness computes, so regret is 0 by construction for a correct pick
evaluation.holdout: the full 1,081, not the 150-example pre-check sample
